articles.title: 8 Years Later, the Most-Near-Perfect Mystery Thriller of the Century is Officially Free on Streaming
articles.summary: Everybody loves a twisty paranoid thriller. The ‘70s embraced gritty conspiracy stories like Three Days of the Condor (1975) and Soylent Green (1973), while contemporary movies like Watcher (2022) and Coherence (2013) bring intriguing new ideas to the genre.
body: Under the Silver Lake pokes fun at the obsessive puzzle-solving tendencies of Sam (Andrew Garfield), an aimless 30-something who involves himself in a bizarre conspiracy that unfolds in Silver Lake, Los Angeles. Despite being days away from being evicted, Sam is more preoccupied with dubious codes, unlikely treasure maps, and flimsy coincidence — anything that his conspiracy-addled brain can make sense of.

After flirting with his neighbor Sarah (Riley Keough), who disappears around the same time as billionaire Jefferson Sevence (Chris Gann), Sam embarks on a quest with no end in sight. Determined to find out what happened to Sarah, Sam attempts to expose Hollywood’s seedy underbelly, convinced that interconnected subliminal messages lie in plain sight. As Sam races from one unlikely location to the next, we’re left to wonder whether his hyperfixations have any basis in reality, or if they’re simply the product of an idle, disillusioned mind.

articles.title: Left 4 Dead 2 Dev Admits Valve Intentionally Leaked Its Own Trailer After the ESRB Blocked It from Release
articles.summary: Former Valve writer Chet Faliszek has a confession to make: Valve intentionally leaked its own Left 4 Dead 2 trailer. The Half-Life and Portal veteran spilled the beans on the studio's past unconventional marketing tactics in a new video uploaded to his YouTube channel (via Ars Technica ).
body: So, why are we just hearing about this now? Well, it's been a few years since any of this would have mattered.

"I think we can't get in trouble for that now. It was like 20 years ago," Faliszek said. "It's funny seeing leaked stuff now because, yeah, I don't think you can look for 'leaked Left 4 Dead 2 trailer' because it's just going to be lost."

Leaks can happen for a variety of reasons. Sometimes companies are hacked and have their content spilled out onto the internet; sometimes someone says something they shouldn't, and sometimes materials are mistakenly published early. Most developers and publishers have their own process to ensure leaks don't happen, but in the case of Left 4 Dead 2, Valve saw opportunity.

articles.title: Netflix's Near-Perfect 9-Part Gothic Thriller Is So Good You'll Finish in One Weekend
articles.summary: Gothic stories have a long shelf life. First published hundreds of years ago and tackling numerous topics, the earliest gothic books and novellas are often packed with ambiance: old and creaky manors, moody weather, hauntings, romantic twists, and longing amid the stress of a hysterical era.
body: In recent years, Mike Flanagan has come out as a leading figure in the realm of adaptations and horror stories, adapting various Stephen King novels to great success along with several original movies and shows. His first big break came in 2018 when he started an anthology series based on classical horror works. The Haunting of Hill House, adapted from the landmark Shirley Jackson novel, was the first — and it quickly became a Netflix phenomenon. Two years later, Flanagan followed it with The Haunting of Bly Manor, a smaller and weirder story that drew inspiration from Henry James’ “The Turn of the Screw,” one of the most adapted novellas in history.
As summer ends and Halloween draws closer, there's no better way to ease into spooky season than by revisiting The Haunting of Bly Manor, either one episode at a time or in a single weekend binge.

articles.title: Insomniac Clears the Air After Marvel's Wolverine Fans Confuse Lady Deathstrike for Psylocke
articles.summary: Insomniac Games has cleared the air after a new trailer for Marvel's Wolverine had fans confusing Lady Deathstrike for Psylocke. If you thought the launch trailer for the PlayStation 5-exclusive video game would come and go without controversy, I've got bad news.
body: In comments across YouTube, Instagram, X/Twitter, and other social media platforms, you don't have to look too hard to find watchers questioning if the sneering villain featured in the launch trailer was Psylocke. Psylocke is an energy-wielding mutant who's been known to show up across various X-Men stories in the past, so when a glowing sword showed up in Marvel's Wolverine, many believed it to be tied to a grand character reveal.
Well, it's not, and Insomniac has done its best to make that clear.

The post above was published earlier today and labels the sword user as Lady Deathstrike. The PlayStation developer didn't outright say it's trying to quiet the noise that's emerged in the days following the trailer's reveal, but judging by the comments, many are shocked any clarification was needed in the first place.
"The fact it has to be stated is so crazy to me," one user said. "Larp monsters are everywhere."

articles.title: 30 Years Later, The X-Files' Most Terrifying Episode Is Still a Top 5 All-Time Sci-Fi Achievement
articles.summary: Created by Chris Carter, The X-Files was a 1990s series about two FBI agents named Fox Mulder (David Duchovny) and Dana Scully (Gillian Anderson) who investigate cases involving paranormal phenomena.
body: Over 11 seasons, the way The X-Files managed to stay fresh was by telling a wide variety of television stories. The show might be about aliens for one week and then follow that up with an urban legend before pivoting to a story about the occult. The show also managed to switch up its genre of stories. While sci-fi was especially prominent, The X-Files managed the occasional comedic episode and sometimes explored outright horror. It was during one of those horror episodes in season 4 that The X-Files writers Glen Morgan and James Wong, along with director Kim Manners, crafted the show’s scariest, most disturbing episode (and one of the most unsettling hours of broadcast television ever).

articles.title: Zach Cregger Says He's Done With Franchise Films After Resident Evil
articles.summary: Resident Evil movie director Zach Cregger is days away from his survival horror adaptation's theatrical premiere, but don't expect him to help bring another franchise film to the big screen ever again.
body: The filmmaker behind this month's Capcom project talked about what's next for him during a conversation with Deadline. When asked if he's ever been pressured to spearhead another recognizable IP, he gave a blunt answer: "I'm not doing that."

"I have never been approached by another franchise," Cregger said. "Maybe I have, but it would never get to me because I have been very clear that I’m not doing that. I’m doing this, and that’s it for me."

One might suspect Cregger's aversion to big franchise films like Resident Evil might stem from the backlash he's received in the months leading up to his movie's premiere. While the Barbarian and Weapons creator certainly has plenty of defenders looking forward to seeing his new live-action take, there have been many, many others who aren't quite as excited.

Most of the pressure has come from those who feel his Resident Evil doesn't align with the game it's based on. Changes to the source material, including its modern setting and snowy Raccoon City, have set fans on edge, while others aren't in love with the idea of following a new protagonist (Austin Abrams' Bryan Hodukavich) instead of someone like Leon S. Kennedy or Claire Redfield.

articles.title: Fire Emblem Fortune's Weave Owes Everything to an Overlooked 3DS Masterpiece
articles.summary: Fire Emblem loves looking back. Fire Emblem Awakening, the Nintendo 3DS title that rescued the franchise from permanent retirement, is packed with references to the series’ history: one character adopts the name Marth, another shouts the names of previous Fire Emblem games on critical hits, and a…
body: Fire Emblem Engage took Awakening’s emphasis on the series’ legacy to an extreme. Though released three years after Fire Emblem’s 30th birthday, it functions as an anniversary game. Core to Engage’s story and gameplay are Emblem Rings, which summon the spirits of practically every notable protagonist of Fire Emblem’s seventeen games.

But for a series so invested in its own history, Intelligent Systems has remade only three Fire Emblem games: twice for the DS and once for the 3DS. That 3DS game, Fire Emblem Echoes: Shadows of Valentia, remakes 1992’s Fire Emblem Gaiden, the second-ever Fire Emblem game. Like fellow early Nintendo sequels Super Mario Bros 2 and Zelda 2: The Adventure of Link, Gaiden stands out against the rest of its series. Features like open exploration, dungeon crawling, and controlling two separate armies would remain unique to Gaiden for decades.

articles.title: Ex-BioWare designer says doom and gloom about the next Mass Effect is overstated: 'I think that they can do it'
articles.summary: Given that Anthem and Mass Effect Andromeda were widely considered disappointments, and Dragon Age: The Veilguard had a divisive reception, there's a certain amount of skepticism about the Mass Effect game BioWare is currently working on. Some have even suggested it might not come out at all.
body: Armando Troisi, a cinematic designer on the Mass Effect trilogy and lead cinematic designer on Mass Effect 2, thinks it's all a bit much. "I think BioWare, when they break it down and do that singleplayer, interactive narrative-driven, deep combat, progression-driven game, really, there's nobody that can touch them," Troisi told FRVR. "It's kind of like the [Master] Chief, it's like going on a walkabout and finding themselves and coming back. I think BioWare can do it if we just leave them alone to do what they do best."

Troisi said that when he was working at BioWare the studio knew what kind of game it was best at making, and that all they need is to get back to that. "The vision was always clear," he said. "There was a BioWare formula and they were going to iterate on that formula and keep turning out best-in-class cinematic RPGs and that's basically what the mandate was. And then they had to live through the live service era—which is still happening but is maybe not as prevalent—and we're all beholden to companies and stakeholders and all the rest of that."

articles.title: Xbox Cloud Gaming's new hourly cap is reportedly set exactly where Microsoft stops making money on it
articles.summary: A new report suggests that Xbox has capped its cloud gaming usage to 15 hours for Game Pass Ultimate subscribers because that's when the service stops being profitable.
body: According to Windows Central, which cites unnamed Microsoft sources, that's not an arbitrary cap and is, allegedly, set at Microsoft's own break-even threshold as any usage beyond that costs the company money.

Windows Central ties the cost pressure to a wider squeeze on server memory caused by Microsoft's AI investments, with Azure capacity increasingly prioritised for AI workloads over game streaming. It frames the caps as part of a broader cost-cutting pattern across Xbox, alongside recent layoffs and cancelled projects, as the division comes under pressure to turn a bigger profit.

As Connor reported for us in the week, according to a 2025 report from Statista, US gamers spent an average of 9.5 hours per week playing video games, UK gamers 6.38 hours, and a worldwide average of 6.56 hours was recorded.
Despite Xbox scaling back its cloud gaming plans and the seemingly endless issues caused by the ramping up of AI data centres, industry giants remain bullish on cloud gaming.

articles.title: Peak studio Aggro Crab is publishing a sick-looking platformer about a blue collar guy doing dirty work on an alien world
articles.summary: At the Game Developers Conference earlier this year, Aggro Crab developer Nick Kaman told me that he thinks there's a lot of meat left on the bone when it comes to co-op " friendslop " games, and that he wants to keep working in the space.
body: It's tough enough to stand out in the games market these days, let alone as a 2D platformer, so I'm always excited when one really breaks through and catches my eye. Rebounder is killing it on the art front, presenting everything in this color-limited, comic book, cel-shadey view that I really dig. It dovetails with the story and designs, a sort of blue collar, working class sci-fi reminiscent of Scavenger's Reign, Alien, or Mouthwashing.

"On a remote lunar worksite, valuable resources from an ancient age flow underfoot, and shareholders demand extraction," reads Rebounders' synopsis on Steam. "Contract workers fly-in and fly-out; blue collar labourers from around the galaxy all trekking to the edges of civilization for the next gig.

"A Rebounder runs lines. They pull up their boots each day and speed through hazardous terrain to deliver precious cargo from point A to point B by any means necessary. It’s the gnarliest trade in the universe."

articles.title: Saber CCO says the studio isn't changing up its comms strategy after recent controversies: 'There's always some dust up'
articles.summary: In a recent interview with PC Gamer's Joshua Wolens at this year's Gamescom, Saber Interactive CCO Tim Willits admitted the studio's leadership had a reputation for saying precisely what it means—"sometimes we 'say what we mean' too much," he laughed.
body: "I've been in the industry for so long, and there's always some dust up," Willits explained. "People got mad at Saber because we put World War Z on Epic, and people were like, 'oh, Saber's destroying the industry.' Now 30 million people have played World War Z. And the games will speak for themselves, even in our experiment with Rideshare [Stimulator]."

If you haven't been keeping up with the latest drama Saber Interactive has courted, here's the skinny: former Saber Interactive writer Stella Sacco claimed she was fired and replaced with AI during the development of Rideshare Stimulator.

Saber's comms department initially put out a fairly benign statement disputing the details of the claim, but CEO Matt Karch subsequently issued a statement to This Week In Videogames that was both aggressively pro-AI, and personally insulting to Sacco.
Karch apologized privately to Sacco before releasing a statement reflecting on the incident which itself contained a targeted barb for a different games industry writer that has since been edited.

articles.title: Sony clarifies PlayStation disc production is dropping by 10 percent in 2028, not to 10 percent
articles.summary: Sony has pushed back on a wave of reports suggesting PlayStation disc manufacturing is about to be gutted by 90 percent after comments from a Sony DADC executive were allegedly misunderstood.
body: According to Game, which went directly to Sony Digital Audio Disc Corporation (DADC) for clarity, output is actually expected to dip by 10 percent in 2028, not to 10 percent.

"To clarify and avoid any misleading information: in that statement Dietmar anticipated an overall product volume decline by 10 percent, not a decline down to 10 percent," a Sony DADC spokesperson told Game, referring to comments made by DADC chief Dietmar Tanzer to an Austrian broadcaster in July.
The spokesperson didn't say what happens beyond 2028, and directed further questions on reorders to PlayStation's own PR team, which didn't respond to Game's queries.

The confusion stems from PlayStation's July announcement that it will stop producing physical discs for new games from January 2028 onward, though already-released titles and games still slated for disc release before that date aren't affected, and reorders will continue afterwards.

articles.title: Dwarf Fortress co-creator Tarn Adams was amazed other devs had heard of his game the first time he went to a convention: 'I didn't know that anyone knew what we were doing'
articles.summary: Dwarf Fortress is a bit like caviar—not everyone's into it, but the people who are describe their experiences with it like a religious awakening. But the game's legendary co-creator, Tarn Adams, didn't even know it had a big following for many years, as he told PC Gamer's Joshua Wolens in a recent…
body: "It was something like 2013, 14 going to PAX in Seattle, and there was an indie mega booth at the time," he recalled. "Of the 50 or 60 games showing—I'm just ballparking the numbers—I'd say 90% of them heard of Dwarf Fortress and also had a very amazed fan-ish response when we were introduced." It was the first time Adams had a sense of the reach his game had.

"That was crazy. I had no idea that that was even a thing," he said. "I didn't know that anyone knew what we were doing … I enjoyed it. I try to have good moral qualities, but I am apparently subject to all forms of flattery and vanity and such."

If he could go back in time, he wouldn't so as to not "disrupt the timeline." But if he could go back in time without the risk of doing that, Adams said might encourage himself to evangelize the game more in its early days.

"I'd probably be more confident about getting it in front of more people sooner. I didn't know the people to do that, though, so I'd probably be like 'go meet some more people,'" he said. "From the release of the game in 2006 up until around 2013, I didn't meet another game developer really, except maybe one or two at a Dwarf Fortress-specific meet."

articles.title: Before HBO’s The Last Of Us, An Entirely Different Adaptation Was Proposed
articles.summary: Naughty Dog's first effort to adapt The Last of Us for the screen was not as an HBO TV show, but a movie, a fact that recently began doing the rounds again on social media.
body: While not everyone agrees with the creative departures from the source material for the TV series on HBO, it's undeniably a success and one of HBO's biggest hits lately. Let's look back at how The Last of Us originated as a movie and run through the key developments that led to it becoming a TV show.
People across X recently discovered a post from Sony Pictures in 2014 declaring that The Last of Us was "soon to be a major motion picture."

This was a real, studio-sponsored image, not a fan mock-up. There was officially produced key art, showing Ellie wielding a knife. There was a "secret panel" at San Diego Comic-Con that year featuring director Sam Raimi, who was originally attached to produce the movie, having already had huge success at Sony with his Spider-Man films.
That The Last of Us was originally going to be a movie is not surprising given how many video game movies came before it and how many have been released since (with varying degrees of success).

videos.title: Elden Ring Tarnished Edition - Switch 2 Tech Review - PS4 Visuals With Boosted Res & Frame-Rates
videos.summary: Digital Foundry is now fully independent! Join the DF Supporter Program and support the team:
body: The complete Elden Ring package lands on Switch 2. Visually speaking we're getting a match for the last-gen PS4 release in core settings - though as a plus, Switch 2's frame-rate exceeds that older Sony release, while its resolution locks at the target 1080p more consistently. Comparisons against Series S are less flattering meanwhile. The lack of DLSS is also perhaps a missed opportunity, but on the whole Nintendo's handheld puts in a robust rendition of a true From Software classic.

videos.summary: SlashZero is a 3D side-scrolling action roguelike game.
body: As a player, you will become a time hacker and be able to traverse across multiple timelines.
Make full use of your action skills and combat strategies, collect items, hunt for clues, piece together the truth, and bring down the final boss!
The feel of the controls, the build configuration, and every aspect of the combat are entirely up to you!
